newsitem.title: USA: Jobless rate edges lower in February.
newsitem.headline: Jobless rate edges lower in February.

text.p: The unemployment rate edged lower last month to 5.3 percent as the economy created more jobs than it has since last spring, the government said Friday, in the government's first reading of the nation's economic health in February.
The Labour Department reported that a whopping 339,000 non-farm jobs were created, the most since May, after payrolls rose by a revised 247,000 in January.
Economists surveyed by Reuters had forecast an unemployment rate of 5.3 percent, down from 5.4 percent in January, and an increase of 230,000 in non-farm payrolls.

"Needless to say, it's stronger than expected. Just about every sector of the report on the surface shows renewed momentum in job creation," said economist Kevin Flanagan, of Dean Witter Reynolds Inc. "You're seeing wage pressures developing and the work week came back in a major way.
Much of the February payrolls increase occurred in the construction sector, which added 109,000 new jobs.

"The magnitude of February's increase can be attributed largely to mild weather across much of the country, following unusually severe weather in January," said Katharine Abraham, commissioner of the department's Bureau of Labour Statistics.
The Labour Department's household survey last month showed the number of job holders falling by 150,000 to 128.43 million, while the number of unemployed workers fell by 63,000 to 7.2 million.
The department's survey of businesses showed strong growth in the services industry, which added 80,000 jobs.

"It's not a report that seems explosive, but it does suggest the economy is still on a roll and leaves very much open the question of whether it's on too fast a roll," said Robert Dederick of Northern Trust.

The benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury bond fell immediately after the report was issued but then rebounded, adding a third of a point. Its yield, which moves in the opposite direction, slipped to 6.86 percent from 6.88 percent Thursday.
Average hourly wages climbed 3 cents last month to $12.09, after edging up a revised 2 cents in January, the department said.
The percentage of unemployed Americans who have left their jobs voluntarily fell to 10.9 percent in February

Job leavers as a percentage of the unemployed had climbed to 12.3 percent in January from 11.7 percent in December -- a fact noted by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan in his recent testimony to Congress.

The Fed chief warned that January's jump in voluntary job leavers may have signalled an end to an unusual period of worker insecurity that had helped keep a lid on wage demands. Financial markets were watching the figure closely amid concerns that signs of growing wage pressures may prompt the Fed to raise interest rates.
Greenspan recently warned that the Fed may decide to raise interest rates to keep the economy from overheating as it nears the end of its sixth year of uninterrupted expansion.

The manufacturing sector lost 2,000 jobs in February after creating 16,000 jobs in January, the department said. Factory overtime hours were up at 4.7 hours per week, while the factory work week rose to 41.9 hours.
